name: Barbell Curl
summary: A classic standing curl that loads both arms evenly and lets you use heavier weights than most biceps exercises. Builds the biceps and the muscles that bend the elbow.
setup: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and take an underhand grip on the bar, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Let the bar hang at thigh level with elbows beside your ribs and a soft knee bend.
Brace your abs and pull the shoulder blades slightly down and back.
execution: Curl the bar up by bending only at the elbows, keeping the upper arms nearly still.
Continue until the forearms are close to vertical and the biceps are fully shortened, without lifting the shoulders.
Pause briefly, then lower the bar over about 2-3 seconds to full arm extension.
Exhale as you curl up and inhale on the way down.
mistakes: Swinging the torso to move the bar: lower the weight and keep your glutes and abs tight.
Elbows drifting far forward: keep them beside the ribs so the biceps, not the shoulders, do the work.
Cutting the bottom short: lower until the arms are almost straight on every rep.
Bending the wrists back under load: keep the wrists neutral in line with the forearms.
